title: Normal liver: sagittal ultrasound
summary: Normal liver parenchyma in a sagittal ultrasound view.
text: The liver is shown in a sagittal view at the midclavicular line. Identify the gray hepatic parenchyma beneath the curved superficial scan boundary.
reading: Follow the sagittal view through the hepatic tissue.

questions.prompt: Which organ contains the labeled parenchyma?
questions.explanation: The labeled tissue is hepatic parenchyma.

labels.note: Hepatic tissue in the sagittal scan.
Echogenic curved diaphragmatic surface beneath the liver dome; identification by position only.

title: Focal hepatic steatosis: ultrasound
summary: An echogenic focus of hepatic steatosis surrounds a traversing vein.
text: The bright hepatic focus illustrates focal steatosis. A hepatic vein passes through the focus without compression. Preserved vessel course favors focal fat in this example; it does not independently exclude every hepatic mass.
reading: Locate the brighter hepatic focus beneath the arrow.
Follow the dark traversing vein through the focus.

questions.prompt: Which feature favors focal steatosis in this example?
options: A traversing hepatic vein remains uncompressed
questions.explanation: The hepatic vein retains its course through the echogenic focus.

labels.note: Echogenic focal hepatic tissue (focal fatty change) beneath the arrow.
A dark vein courses through the focus without compression.

title: Normal adult kidney: longitudinal ultrasound
summary: Cortex, pyramid and renal sinus in a normal adult kidney.
text: The kidney is shown along its long axis. Three asterisks mark the cortex, two mark a pyramid, and four mark the renal sinus. The central sinus is brighter than the surrounding renal parenchyma.
reading: Find the cortex at the triple-asterisk marker.
Compare the pyramid with the brighter renal sinus.

questions.prompt: Which structure is marked by four asterisks?
questions.explanation: Four asterisks mark the bright central renal sinus.

labels.note: Outer renal parenchyma at the triple-asterisk marker.
Renal pyramid at the double-asterisk marker.
Bright central renal sinus at the quadruple-asterisk marker. The atlas has no sinus fat, so the hilar renal veins stand in for it.
Anechoic renal pelvis and calyceal urine at the centre of the sinus; dark on ultrasound.

title: Hydronephrosis with cortical atrophy: ultrasound
summary: Dilated anechoic renal pelvis and calyces with cortical atrophy.
text: Hydronephrosis expands the dark renal pelvis and calyces. Cortical atrophy accompanies the collecting-system dilatation in this example. The image alone does not establish the cause or duration of obstruction.
reading: Identify the expanded dark collecting-system spaces.
Locate the dilated calyx between the calipers.
Compare the collecting system with the separate normal kidney image.

questions.prompt: What is the dark space between the calipers?
questions.explanation: The anechoic calyx is enlarged as part of the hydronephrosis.

labels.note: Anechoic collecting-system space between the calipers, part of the hydronephrosis.
Anechoic renal pelvis expanded by urine; the dilatation is the pathology on this image.

title: Gallstones and biliary sludge: ultrasound
summary: Echogenic gallstones and sludge within the gallbladder.
text: Gallstones and sludge occupy the dependent part of the gallbladder. Echogenic stones produce posterior acoustic shadowing. This example is described as cholelithiasis without current cholecystitis; a single image does not replace the complete clinical and ultrasound assessment.
reading: Find the bright dependent gallstones and the mixed echoes of sludge.

questions.prompt: Which finding is present in the dependent gallbladder?
questions.explanation: The dependent bright calculi and mixed echoes illustrate gallstones and sludge.

labels.note: Bright dependent stones within the gallbladder, with posterior acoustic shadowing.
Fluid-filled gallbladder above the dependent material.
Bright echogenic anterior wall of the gallbladder.
Adjacent liver parenchyma beside the gallbladder.

title: Femoral-vein thrombosis: color Doppler ultrasound
summary: Echogenic thrombus and absent color flow in the femoral vein.
text: The femoral vein contains echogenic thrombus and lacks the color filling seen in the neighboring femoral artery and deep femoral vein. The femoral vein belongs to the deep venous system. A static Doppler image does not demonstrate a compression examination.
reading: Compare the middle femoral vein with the color-filled vessels above and below it.
Locate the thrombus within the femoral vein.

questions.prompt: Which vessel contains the thrombus in this image?
questions.explanation: The middle femoral vein contains echogenic material and lacks color filling.

labels.note: Echogenic material in the femoral vein without color filling.

title: Bilateral renal calculi: abdominal radiograph
summary: Renal calculi in both upper abdominal renal regions.
text: Bilateral renal calculi appear as radiopaque foci in the upper abdomen. Rounded pelvic calcifications represent phleboliths and should be distinguished from the renal calculi. The radiograph does not establish urinary obstruction or renal function.
reading: Locate calculi in both upper abdominal renal regions.
Compare their location with the rounded pelvic phlebolith.

questions.prompt: Which finding should be distinguished from renal calculi?
questions.explanation: The separate rounded pelvic calcifications are phleboliths.

labels.note: Radiopaque calculus in the right upper abdominal renal region (patient right; image left).
Radiopaque calculus in the left upper abdominal renal region (patient left; image right).
Rounded venous calcification in the pelvic venous plexus. Distinct from the renal calculi; not in the urinary tract.
Lumbar vertebral bodies outlined on the frontal film; the renal calculi lie lateral to the spine.
